predictions.title: Cross-orchestrator interop matrix ships five-surface mitigation by Q3 2026
predictions.body: By Q3 2026 the six-vendor cross-orchestrator interop matrix reaches general availability shipping the full five-surface agent-loader mitigation set on by default, turning the verification baseline that has so far lived in changelogs and reference implementations into a portable conformance contract that holds the same across every major agentic-orchestration product. The Monday catalysts are concrete and converge on a settling integration rather than a fresh feature. Mistral's Monday Workflows note confirms the five-vendor cross-orchestrator interop matrix — Codex CLI plus Claude Code 3.0 plus Mistral Workflows plus Azure AI Foundry plus Vertex AI Agent Governance Center plus Amazon Bedrock Agent Registry — holds its first-week-of-June general-availability target, shipping the five-surface signed-checkpoint plus manifest-allowlist plus workflow-state plus intermediate-state-serializer plus nested-dependency-resolution canonicalization mitigation set as a default with support for all fifteen-jurisdiction Indo-Pacific tenant-policy field schemas. A Monday InfoQ note reports the interop-matrix conformance test suite holding green across all participating vendors as the weekday integration cycle resumed, with no schema-drift regression, and OpenAI's Monday Codex CLI v3.1.5 point release consolidates its client-side mitigation surface explicitly ahead of the early-June matrix general-availability target. A Monday vLLM blog release note cuts v0.11.4 stable with the same five-surface mitigation set on by default, and a Monday Hugging Face post confirms the LangChain, AutoGen, CrewAI, Haystack, and Pydantic AI maintainer cohort holding its coordinated mid-June default-shipment commitment covering the identical five surfaces with no schedule revision. The structural force is that once the conformance suite is green across every matrix vendor, each vendor's own client release is consolidating against the same five-surface set, the serving-stack and framework cohorts are both defaulting that exact set inside the same June window, and the matrix already carries the fifteen-jurisdiction tenant-policy schemas, the matrix cannot reach general availability defaulting a partial bundle without breaking the cross-vendor conformance contract its own test suite enforces. The most likely landing is the cross-orchestrator interop matrix reaching general availability in Q3 2026 — most plausibly in the named first-week-of-June window — with all six vendors defaulting the full five-surface mitigation set, the conformance suite cited as the portability guarantee, and per-vendor release notes referencing the consolidated loader-verification baseline. Bear case is that one vendor's general-availability slot slips a sub-minor cycle and the matrix ships five-of-six at the June window with the sixth following inside the quarter; absent that slip, Q3 2026 lands the cross-orchestrator interop matrix shipping the five-surface mitigation as a default.

reasoning.so_that: The interop matrix reaches general availability defaulting the full five-surface mitigation set.
reasoning.landing: By Q3 2026; all six matrix vendors defaulting the five-surface mitigation.
reasoning.plain_language: Six rival AI-agent platforms are wiring their security checks together so a tool stays equally safe whichever platform runs it.

predictions.summary: Monday notes confirm the six-vendor cross-orchestrator interop matrix holds its early-June GA target with a green conformance suite, and the framework and serving cohorts default the same five surfaces. By Q3 2026 the matrix reaches GA defaulting the full five-surface mitigation set.

predictions.title: SambaNova converts its confidential SEC submission to a public S-1 by Q4 2026
predictions.body: By Q4 2026 SambaNova files its confidential SEC draft registration statement publicly as an S-1, putting a third AI-accelerator name into the IPO pipeline behind the now-public Cerebras and the further-along Tenstorrent. The Monday catalysts are concrete and span the filing clock, the comparable, and the sibling pipeline. A Monday HPCwire AIwire note confirms SambaNova's bookrunner roster holding at six with its confidential-submission filing target firmed to the final week of June, the next mechanical step before the SEC Corp Fin review cycle begins. The same note reports Tenstorrent — one filing stage ahead — sitting in the standard staff-review interval after its first-round comment-letter response, holding an early-August public-filing target, which establishes the Corp Fin review cadence a SambaNova submission will track. The valuation comparable an AI-accelerator S-1 must price against has hardened: a Monday BEAMSTART note reports Cerebras CBRS opening the new trading week with a five-desk analyst spread bracketing the stock inside a roughly $185-to-$235 band, institutional-buyside net position near 37 percent of float, and the four-consecutive-day consolidation base treated as the operative public comparable. The AI-accelerator demand backdrop the S-1 will lean on is also advancing on a Monday cadence: AMD's Helios plus MI450 commitment book advanced to near 10.4GW with a fresh sovereign-cloud commitment, and Tenstorrent Wormhole Galaxy rack shipments reached roughly 177 racks against a 280-rack first-half capacity target. The structural force is that once SambaNova's bookrunner roster is locked at six, the confidential-submission target is firmed to a specific late-June week, a sibling filer is already demonstrating the Corp Fin review interval the submission will follow, and a fully analyst-bracketed public comparable plus a hardening accelerator-demand backdrop are both in place, the path from confidential submission to public S-1 compresses to Corp Fin review-window arithmetic — a late-June submission plus the standard first-and-second-round comment-letter cycle lands the public filing inside Q4 2026. The most likely landing is SambaNova making its confidential submission in the final week of June and converting to a public S-1 in Q4 2026, the filing citing the Cerebras post-IPO trading range as its valuation comparable, with Cerebras public and Tenstorrent's earlier public filing keeping a three-name AI-accelerator IPO pipeline visible. Bear case is a capital-markets-window shock or an extended Corp Fin comment cycle that pushes SambaNova's public filing into early 2027; absent that, Q4 2026 lands SambaNova's public S-1 as the pipeline's third AI-accelerator name.

predictions.title: OECD adopts the cyber-evaluation reciprocity attestation schema by Q3 2026
predictions.body: By Q3 2026 the OECD adopts its cyber-evaluation reciprocity attestation field schema as a formal Recommendation, fixing a single cross-jurisdiction data shape for how AI cyber-evaluation results are attested and recognized across the reciprocity perimeter that has otherwise grown candidate by candidate without a common standard. The Monday catalysts are concrete and trace a clearing-procedure sequence. A Monday andrew.ooo procedural note confirms the OECD GENAI working-group secretariat's finalized cyber-evaluation reciprocity attestation field schema draft Recommendation text remains in member-state circulation on schedule for the June 2-6 plenary adoption target, with the secretariat reporting member-state comment submissions on the schema have now passed two-thirds of the named candidate cohort as the business week resumed. A Monday Decoder note reports the cross-jurisdiction reciprocity perimeter holding at fifteen named candidates plus the originating UK and EU, with Qatar's weekend exploratory-observer commitment now in its 270-day national-consultation window and the operational recognition threshold steady at Mythos-class plus GPT-5.5-class capability. On the United States track, the Frontier Model Review Board executive order's classified-annex response clock runs into its third calendar day against a Friday May 22 deadline, with OSTP holding no signing window before May 22 — leaving the order as the cited instrument expected to begin closing the US recognition gap against the perimeter the OECD schema would standardize. The structural force is that once the draft Recommendation text is finalized and circulating on schedule, member-state comment submissions have already cleared two-thirds of the candidate cohort, the plenary adoption target sits on a fixed June 2-6 calendar, and the perimeter has hardened to fifteen-plus jurisdictions all converging on a common attestation shape, adoption compresses to plenary-process arithmetic — comment close plus the standard plenary adoption interval lands the Recommendation inside Q3 2026. The most likely landing is the OECD adopting the cyber-evaluation reciprocity attestation field schema as a formal Recommendation in Q3 2026 — most plausibly at the June 2-6 plenary itself — with the fifteen-plus perimeter jurisdictions referencing the schema as the common attestation contract and the FMRB order cited as the United States' route to recognition under it. Bear case is that residual member-state comments push formal adoption to a post-plenary written-procedure round landing in Q4 2026; absent that, Q3 2026 lands the OECD cyber-evaluation reciprocity attestation Recommendation.

reasoning.because: The OECD's attestation-schema draft Recommendation is circulating on schedule for a June plenary.
reasoning.given: Member-state comments passed two-thirds of the cohort and the perimeter holds at fifteen-plus.
reasoning.so_that: The OECD adopts the cyber-evaluation reciprocity attestation schema as a formal Recommendation.
reasoning.landing: By Q3 2026; OECD Recommendation adopted, most plausibly at the June plenary.
reasoning.plain_language: Many countries are about to agree on one shared form for proving an AI passed its cyber-safety tests, so results count everywhere.

predictions.summary: The OECD's cyber-evaluation reciprocity attestation field schema is circulating on schedule for a June 2-6 plenary, member-state comments have passed two-thirds of the candidate cohort, and the perimeter holds at fifteen-plus jurisdictions. By Q3 2026 the OECD adopts the schema as a Recommendation.
